easy.def: The part of your head that thinks.
examples: Your brain helps you learn.
The brain tells your body what to do.
A brain is in your head.

more.def: The organ inside your head that controls your body and lets you think, feel and remember.
examples: Your brain sends messages to every part of your body.
Reading exercises your brain.
Humans have large brains compared to their size.
The brave girl went down the big slide.
The brave boy got his shot at the doctor.
Firefighters are brave.

more.def: Willing to do something hard or scary even when you feel afraid.
examples: It was brave of him to speak in front of the whole school.
The brave sailor steered the ship through the storm.
She was brave enough to say sorry first.
The glass can break.
I broke a plate.
The stick is broken.

more.def: To come apart or make something come apart, often by hitting or dropping it.
examples: Be careful, or the glass will break on the hard floor.
The toy broke when it fell down the stairs.
He broke the chocolate bar into four pieces.
We take a break.
It is time for a break.
Let us have a break.

more.def: A short rest from work or study.
examples: The class took a break to stretch and drink water.
We stopped for a break halfway up the mountain.
There is no school during the winter break.

easy.def: The first meal of the day.
examples: I eat breakfast at seven.
We have eggs for breakfast.
Breakfast is ready.

more.def: The meal that you eat in the morning.
examples: We had pancakes for breakfast.
She skipped breakfast and ran for the bus.
Breakfast is the first meal of the day.
A cool breeze blew my hair.
The breeze moved the curtains.
My kite flew in the breeze.
A breeze from the sea kept us cool on the hot beach.
The flags waved gently in the morning breeze.
We opened the windows to let the breeze in.
The sun is very bright.
I wear a bright yellow coat.
The lamp is too bright for my eyes.

more.def: Giving off or filled with a lot of light; also, strong in color.
examples: The bright moon lit up the whole field.
Bright stars filled the sky on the clear night.
She painted her room a bright shade of green.

easy.def: To carry something to a place.
examples: Bring your book.
She brought her lunch.
I will bring a toy.

more.def: To carry or lead someone or something to a place.
examples: Please bring your homework to school on Monday.
My aunt brought flowers when she came to visit.
Can you bring the baby her blanket?

easy.def: A boy who has the same parents as you.
examples: My brother is tall.
I play with my brother.
Her brother is five.

more.def: A boy or man who has the same parents as another person.
examples: My older brother taught me how to throw a ball.
She has two brothers, and they love to build forts.
His little brother follows him everywhere.

easy.def: Having the color of chocolate or dirt.
examples: My dog is brown.
Bears have brown fur.
The tree trunk is brown.

more.def: Having the color of soil, wood or chocolate.
examples: The brown leaves crunched under our feet.
She packed her lunch in a brown paper bag.
A brown owl sat quietly in the tree.

easy.def: The color of chocolate or dirt.
examples: Brown is my favorite color.
Mix red and green to make brown.
The cat is mostly brown.

more.def: The color of soil, wood or chocolate.
examples: The room was painted in shades of brown.
Autumn fills the woods with orange, red and brown.
Her eyes are a warm brown.
